subject: Atlantic Health — forgiveness & term-reset approval needed
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Atlantic Health renewal — concession request for exec review

Team,

Quick summary up front: Atlantic Health (regional hospital system, current ARR ~$420k) is signaling churn at renewal unless we agree to a set of concessions. They are a strategic reference with an expansion pipeline (3 more hospitals, ~+$300k ARR projected year 2). Customer deadline: they want terms returned by EOD Apr 8 to stay on track for May 15 renewal.

Customer asks (explicit):
- 30% off list price for the first 12 months
- Term reset to a new 12-month period starting at renewal (effectively pushing next renewal to May 2028)
- SLA addendum that includes a 99.95% availability target plus 1x makegood credit if breached
- One-time onboarding credit to cover integration services (~$10k)

Attachments: Atlantic_SOW_v3.pdf (current draft), usage_breakdown_Q1.xlsx (their token/usage profile).

Why this matters: if we say no, they will evaluate other providers with aggressive pricing. If we concede, we stand to keep current footprint and capture the expansion (~$300k) in year two; loss of reference and expansion could cost >$700k in TCV over two years.

What I am asking from you:
- Executive approval to offer a negotiated concession package (see recommended options below) so we can return a single, signed SOW to the customer by Apr 8.
- Legal/RevOps/Finance to confirm required wording and commercial guardrails.

Recommended options (in priority order):
A) Exec option (preserve account + expansion): 25% first-year discount, 12-month term reset, SLA addendum (limited credits, see proposed language), 1x onboarding credit $7.5k.
B) Middle ground: 15% discount + 12-month term reset + SLA language w/ capped credits + 50% onboarding credit.
C) Minimal: 10% discount + 6-month term reset — acceptable but much higher churn risk.

I think A is the right commercial tradeoff given expansion upside. Requesting explicit signoff from Irene (exec) and alignment from Marissa/David for impact and DocuSign authority.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Atlantic_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: usage_breakdown_Q1.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Atlantic Health renewal — concession request for exec review

Rishi — thanks for the concise ask. A few quick points from RevOps:
- Need a clear P&L impact for each option (A/B/C) and the expected churn probability if we decline.
- If we do a term reset, confirm whether billing cycles change (will impact revenue recognition).
- Who owns the expansion retention clause? We should add a 6-month out clause that requires Atlantic to notify of planned expansion in writing to qualify for the concession.

Can you drop a one-slide financial impact (ARR delta + 12-mo cash impact) into this thread? I’ll also need the final SOW language before DocuSign.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | RevOps Manager
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Atlantic Health renewal — concession request for exec review

Numbers quick and dirty (based on current $420k ARR):
- 30% first-year discount => revenue reduction Y1 = ~$126k (nominal)
- 25% first-year discount => reduction = ~$105k
- 15% first-year discount => reduction = ~$63k

If expansion converts (~$300k ARR in Y2) the LTV favors conceding. Cash timing: a 12-month term reset pushes recognition but not cash unless we change invoicing.

Approval authority: Finance can approve up to 15% ad hoc discount without exec signoff. Anything >15% requires an Exec-level approval and a documented business rationale. SLA credit exposure: need legal to cap credits (recommend cap at 1x monthly recurring revenue per breach, annual cumulative cap of 2x MRR).

Recommendation: Approve option A only with explicit exec signoff and a signed concession amendment that limits SLA exposure and ties discounts to commitment to expand or confirmed purchase order schedule.

-David
David Kim | Head of Finance, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Annette Gomez <annette.gomez@atlantichealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Atlantic Health internal confirmation — customer ready to move if we can meet terms

Looping a snippet of the thread I just got from Annette (customer). They want an answer by Apr 8. If we push to the middle-ground they may still shop. We have verbal confirmation they will sign if we accept A.

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Annette Gomez <annette.gomez@atlantichealth.com>
Date: Sat, Apr 3, 2027 at 07:58 AM -0400
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Subject: RE: Renewal options

Rishi — thanks for the call. We value the product and the team, but budget pressure across the system means we need help to make this work this fiscal year. If Redwood can provide a 30% concession to start with the term reset, and a one-time onboarding credit to cover our professional services, we will sign a final SOW this week and commit to the expansion evaluation immediately.

We need the commitment in writing by Apr 8.

Annette
Procurement Director, Atlantic Health
[Attachment: customer_acceptance_thread.eml (EML)]

Rishi here — I’ve also attached the SOW and our usage files. I appreciate David’s note about the authority cap. Asking for exec support to approve Option A (or at least 25%) to avoid a drawn-out negotiation that risks losing momentum.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call if helpful.
Rishi

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Atlantic Health renewal — concession request for exec review

Thanks for pulling this together and for the clear options. I reviewed the numbers and the expansion potential. Given the strategic value and the concrete expansion signals, I am prepared to approve a constrained concession to preserve the account. Approvals below (conditional):

Approved concession (conditional):
- 25% off list price for first 12 months (not 30%)
- Term reset to a new 12-month period from renewal date
- SLA addendum permitted with credits capped at 1x MRR per incident and cumulative cap of 2x MRR per 12-month period; SLA credit language must be reviewed and approved by Legal
- One-time onboarding credit of $7,500 to offset professional services

Conditions and next steps:
1) Marissa: please produce the concession P&L (ARR delta and cash timing) and an updated SOW that reflects the approved concession language.
2) David: please confirm finance signoff on revenue recognition treatment and finalize billing terms (no change to invoicing cadence unless customer requests).
3) Karthik/Legal: draft concession amendment and SLA addendum; I will sign the concession authority memo once Legal confirms language and RevOps confirms the P&L.
4) Rishi: return signed concession amendment to the customer by Apr 8 and coordinate DocuSign; include a clause that links the concession to a good-faith expansion evaluation (they must provide a written timeline for expansion by end of Q3 2027).

I will not approve a 30% concession at this time. The approved package preserves most of the commercial benefit while keeping SLA exposure contained. Please treat this as an exec-level decision and act quickly.

Irene Choi
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Note: Legal & RevOps to confirm final wording before external sign-off]
